start-event.description: Start events are not allowed in an ad-hoc sub-process. An activity without an incoming sequence flow is enabled immediately when the sub-process starts.

end-event.description: End events are not allowed in an ad-hoc sub-process. Completion is governed by the sub-process completion condition instead.

missing-activity.description: An ad-hoc sub-process must contain at least one activity.

@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/implicit-start.js.description: A flow node without an incoming sequence flow is instantiated when the process starts. Use an explicit start event to improve clarity.

@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/implicit-end.js.description: A flow node without an outgoing sequence flow consumes its token upon completion. Use an explicit end event to improve clarity.

intermediate.description: Intermediate events must be typed to indicate the event that is caught or thrown (although not illegal, an untyped intermediate event would be interpreted as an insufficiently declared throw event).

boundary.description: A boundary event must be typed to indicate the event it catches.

event-sub-process-start.description: A start event of an event sub-process must be typed to indicate the event it catches.
event-sub-process-start.reference: BPMN 2.0.2, Start Events for Event Sub-Processes, p. 241

activity.description: Several unconditional outgoing flows from an activity create a parallel split, sending a token along each. Use an explicit gateway to improve clarity and avoid misinterpretation.

event.description: Several unconditional outgoing flows from an event create a parallel split, sending a token along each. Use an explicit gateway to improve clarity and avoid misinterpretation.

activity.description: Several incoming flows to an activity are uncontrolled, so the activity is instantiated separately for each arriving token without synchronisation. Use an explicit gateway to improve clarity and avoid misinterpretation.

event.description: Several incoming flows to an event are uncontrolled, so the event is enabled separately for each arriving token without synchronisation. Use an explicit gateway to improve clarity and avoid misinterpretation.

conditional.description: A conditional flow out of an activity forms an implicit gateway. Use an explicit gateway to improve clarity.

default.description: A default flow out of an activity forms an implicit gateway. Use an explicit gateway to improve clarity.

@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/cycle.js.description: A cycle in the sequence flow can cause unintended side-effects (e.g. livelock or race hazard). Use a loop activity to guard against such problems.

@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/complex-gateway.js.description: Complex gateways should be avoided and can usually be replaced by a combination of exclusive, parallel, and inclusive gateways.

@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/structural-anomaly..description: The control flow appears to have an overly complex structure that can probably be simplified.

deadlock.description: An exclusive split creates a token on only one outgoing sequence flow, but a parallel join waits for a token on every incoming flow. The join never receives all its tokens, so it blocks and the process deadlocks. Use matching gateway types.

possible-deadlock.description: A branch leading to a parallel join may never receive a token, so the join waits for it forever and the process deadlocks. Use an inclusive merge.

race.description: A parallel split creates a token on each outgoing sequence flow, but an exclusive merge passes on every token it receives. The flow after the merge therefore runs once for each token. Use matching gateway types.

possible-race.description: More than one branch leading to an exclusive merge may receive a token, and the merge passes on each token it receives, so the flow after the merge may run more than once. Use an inclusive merge.

mismatch.description: Avoid inconsistent blocks to improve readability and guard against issues such as deadlocks or race hazards.

overcomplex.description: The control flow could not be reduced to properly nested splits and joins, so its soundness cannot be determined. Simplify it into matching split and join blocks.

@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/non-interrupting-bo.description: Non-interrupting boundary events cause race hazards as they can be triggered multiple times. Consider using a non-interrupting event-subprocess instead.

@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/process-start-event.description: It is discouraged to use multiple start events.

typed-start.description: A sub-process must use a blank start event. Its flow is triggered by the token from the parent process.

multiple-start.description: A sub-process has at most one start event. The token from the parent process triggers it.

empty.description: An empty sub-process has no start event and no content, so there is nothing to execute.

@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/event-sub-process-s.description: An event sub-process must have exactly one start event.
@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/event-sub-process-s.reference: BPMN 2.0.2, Start Events for Event Sub-Processes, p. 241

race.description: Both duplicate flows fire, so the target is reached twice, causing a race. Remove the duplicate.

deadlock.description: A parallel join waits for a token on each duplicate flow, but the source sends only one, so the process deadlocks. Remove the duplicate.

redundant.description: One of the duplicate flows is redundant and never affects the outcome. Remove it.

@bpmn-workbench/bpmn/superfluous-gateway.description: A gateway must have either multiple incoming sequence flows or multiple outgoing sequence flows (i.e., it must merge or split the flow).

engine/non-executable-process.js.description: The engine refuses a model holding a process that is not marked executable, throwing as it reads it, so one unmarked process stops the whole model from loading. The flag is absent by default.

engine/typed-task.js.description: A user, manual, script, business rule or service task runs as an ordinary task: the operators are applied and the timestamp advances by what they compute. Nothing fails, but no script is run, no user is asked and no rule is evaluated, so the model reads as though something happens that does not.

engine/event-type.js.description: A process is started by a blank start event, instantiated as the instance data declares, or by a message or signal start event, instantiated whenever the message or signal triggering it is thrown. A timer or conditional start event of a process the engine refuses when it reads the model; an error or escalation start event it abandons the run at.

engine/process-start-event.js.description: A process has exactly one start event, and which one it is decides how the process is instantiated. The engine throws "process ... has multiple start nodes" where there is more than one, the token at the process creating the state machine for its contents from the one start node it finds.

engine/cancel-event.js.description: Cancel events are parsed and then not executed: a cancel boundary event never fires and a cancel end event departs as an untyped one would, leaving the transaction it was meant to undo untouched.

engine/terminate-event.js.description: Terminate events are parsed and then not executed: a token reaching one departs as it would from an untyped end event, so the other tokens of the process keep running and nothing is terminated.

engine/link-event.js.description: Link events are parsed and then not executed: the token departs the source along its outgoing flows and never arrives at the target, so a model relying on a link to continue elsewhere loses the token instead.

engine/multiple-event-definitions.js.description: An event is what its one event definition says it is. The engine refuses a model in which an event carries several, throwing as it reads it, for a boundary, a catching and a throwing event alike. A model needing an event triggered by whichever of several occurs first states one event per definition and joins them at an event-based gateway.

engine/call-activity.js.description: Calling a process is not embedding one: a call activity derives from Activity rather than SubProcess and the engine names it nowhere, so a token reaching one has neither contents to run nor a completion to wait for. A model needing the called process executed embeds it as a sub-process.

engine/transaction.js.description: A transaction runs as an ordinary sub-process: its contents execute and it completes. What does not happen is what makes it a transaction, the engine naming no cancel event, so it cannot be cancelled and its completed activities are never compensated on cancellation. Work to be undone is declared as compensation instead.

engine/inclusive-gateway.js.description: The execution engine does not run inclusive gateways: it merges only a parallel join and splits only parallel and event-based gateways, and fails when it reaches an inclusive one.

timestampMissing.description: The engine reads the first status attribute of a process as the timestamp the token stands at, moving the one with the id Timestamp there as it reads the model. A process declaring none does not fail: whatever it declared first is read as the timestamp instead.

instanceMissing.description: The engine reads the first data attribute of a process as the instance identifier, moving the one with the id Instance there as it reads the model. A process declaring none does not fail: whatever it declared first is read as the identifier instead.

instanceAssigned.description: An operator may never assign the instance identifier. The engine refuses such a model as it reads it.

timestampAdvanced.description: An operator may advance the timestamp only where the element takes time. The operators of a process or a sub-process are applied at its start event, which is instantaneous, and a send, receive or decision task completes upon an event of its own, so none of them may. The engine refuses such a model as it reads it.

timestampReceived.description: A message or signal content written into the timestamp moves the token in time as the content is applied. The engine permits it, refusing only a content written into a data or global attribute, so nothing else reports it.

bpmnos/attribute-redeclared.js.description: An attribute must not be declared twice at one element, nor redeclare an id or a name it inherits. An id is the key every lookup is built on and is unique within the process declaring it; a repeated name shadows the other attribute for every expression in this scope, and the engine refuses to load a model where one name denotes two attributes visible at a node.

bpmnos/attribute-undeclared.js.description: An attribute named by a message or signal content must be declared at the node or inherited by it. Attributes used inside expressions (restrictions, operators, conditions, parameter values) are not checked here: the engine compiles those and rejects unknown names itself.

objectiveWithoutWeight.description: An attribute contributing to the objective needs a weight: the weight is the factor of its term, the objective its sign. The engine rejects the model without one.

weightWithoutObjective.description: A weight without an objective has nothing to scale. The engine rejects the model; state minimize or maximize, or drop the weight.

unknownObjective.description: An objective must be minimize, maximize or none. The engine rejects anything else.

missing.description: Every non-default outgoing flow of a diverging exclusive or inclusive gateway needs a gatekeeper: it is what decides whether the branch is taken. An exclusive gateway takes the first flow whose conditions hold and fails outright at a flow that states none.

unused.description: A gatekeeper is consulted only for the non-default outgoing flows of a diverging exclusive or inclusive gateway. Anywhere else the flow is taken without being asked: a single outgoing flow is always taken, the default flow is taken when no other applies, and a parallel or event-based gateway copies the token to all of its flows.

timer.description: A timer event must state when it fires: a bpmnos:timer parameter giving the trigger. Without it the engine never schedules the event.

condition.description: A conditional event must state what it waits for: at least one bpmnos:restriction. Without it the engine never triggers the event.

signal.description: A signal event must state which signal it is: a bpmnos:signal giving the name. A signal is matched by its name alone, so the engine refuses a model that omits it.

bpmnos/signal-self-trigger.js.description: A process throwing the signal its own start event declares instantiates itself. The engine permits this, a signal being broadcast without a sender, so a re-throw guarded by a base case is legitimate and an unguarded one does not terminate.

bpmnos/adhoc-operators.js.description: The operators of a scope are applied to the token at its start event. An ad-hoc sub-process has none, so operators declared for it are never applied.

noLoopCharacteristics.description: Loop parameters are read only for an activity BPMN marks as a standard loop or as multi-instance. Without those markers the engine does not loop and ignores the parameters.

unknownParameter.description: A loop parameter must be named cardinality, index, condition or maximum. The engine ignores any other name.

unusedParameter.description: A multi-instance activity is sized by cardinality and may name an index; a standard loop repeats while condition holds, up to maximum iterations counted in index. A parameter belonging to the other kind of loop is never read.

duplicateParameter.description: The same loop parameter given twice: the engine keeps the last one and discards the earlier.

parameterWithoutValue.description: A loop parameter must carry the expression the engine evaluates. Without a value it is skipped.

noCardinality.description: A multi-instance activity is sized by its cardinality. Without one, the engine creates no instances and fails when the activity is reached.

maximumWithoutIndex.description: A loop maximum bounds the loop index, so the activity must name an index attribute to count in. Without it the engine fails when the activity is entered.

illegalValue.description: A header parameter states the name of a declared attribute or a quoted string. The engine needs the type of every header entry when it reads the model, and only these two state one: an unquoted string names no attribute, and an expression states a value whose type follows from a run. A parameter without a value is permitted and means that the entry holds no value, which every value held under that name matches.

identifierNotString.description: The header entries name, sender and recipient hold a message name and the instance identifiers of the sending and the receiving token, so a parameter stating one of them states a string.

triggerHeader.description: A message instantiating a process is matched by its name alone, the instance not existing before it arrives, so a header entry is never read. The start event states no parameter at all; an element throwing such a message states no key beyond name, sender and recipient, a key the start event cannot match preventing the two from ever being paired.

triggerRecipient.description: A message instantiating a process states no recipient: the instance it is delivered to does not exist until the message creates it.

noMessage.description: A message event exchanges the message it defines, so an event without a bpmnos:message exchanges nothing.

noRecipient.description: A message is delivered only to an event the engine pairs with the sender, which requires the same message name, the same header keys holding values of the same type, and message flows permitting the pair. A message no catching event is paired with is never delivered, whatever a run computes. Whether the values of a header agree is decided by a run and is not checked here.

noSender.description: A message is received only from an event the engine pairs with the recipient, which requires the same message name, the same header keys holding values of the same type, and message flows permitting the pair. A message no throwing event is paired with is never received, whatever a run computes. Whether the values of a header agree is decided by a run and is not checked here.

triggerCaughtElsewhere.description: A message instantiating a process is matched by its name alone, so no element other than that start event may catch a message of that name: a second one would be a choice the engine has no decision in which to make. Several elements may throw it, each instantiating a process of its own.
